audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says Tryndamere wants to "Use Mocking Shout to slow Tahm Kench and create the spacing needed to kite". Mocking Shout's slow only applies to enemies whose backs are turned to him — the attack-damage reduction hits everyone, the slow does not.
audit.why: This inverts the counterplay. Tahm Kench's whole plan is to walk forward into Tongue Lash range; facing Tryndamere means the slow half of Mocking Shout never touches him. It is the disengage that gets punished, not the approach — which also means running away from a Tryndamere is the single worst response to hearing it.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (14s): -bonus AD for 4s on everyone, plus a 3.25s curse that slows only while you are facing away. Walk at him, not off him.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says swallowing a Tryndamere in Undying Rage "means five seconds of him regenerating Bloodlust stacks inside your belly". The real reason is simpler and sharper: Devour holds a champion for up to 3 seconds and Undying Rage runs for 5, and Undying Rage can be cast while stunned or suppressed.
audit.why: The stated reason is invented mechanics. The true numbers give the player a rule they can count: you can never out-hold a Rage, and he can press R after you have already eaten him, so the swallow has to happen before the button, not after.
audit.corrected: Devour holds up to 3 seconds. Undying Rage lasts 5 and casts through cast-inhibiting crowd control, including your suppression.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] and whys[4] both tell the player to "track the 100-second window" on Undying Rage. That is the rank-2 number only — it is 120/100/80s.
audit.why: At level 6 the cooldown is 120 seconds, so a player counting 100 walks into a lane where he believes R is back twenty seconds before it is. Nothing else is also missing here: Spinning Slash's 12/11/10/9/8s cooldown drops 1.5 seconds for every crit he lands on a champion, so in a long fight his escape comes back far faster than the base number implies.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage 120/100/80s. Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8s, reduced 1.5s per crit on a champion (0.75s on anything else).
sources: League Wiki — Tryndamere: Undying Rage, Spinning Slash

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] ("Lvl 2-3"), early and whys[1]/whys[2] all describe finishing the combo with Devour at levels 2-3. Devour is the ultimate and is not available until 6.
audit.why: It sells a kill pattern that cannot be cast for another three or four levels, which is the difference between a chunk trade and walking into a fight you have no finisher for.
audit.corrected: Levels 2-3 are the 1.5s Tongue Lash stun and the auto chain that follows. Devour joins at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] claims Spinning Slash "resets the An Acquired Taste stack count".
audit.why: Nothing Tryndamere casts touches your stacks. They fall off on their own — 5 seconds after the last application, then one stack per 0.67s. The practical advice is the same shape but the mechanism matters: he is not removing stacks, he is stalling until they expire, which means the answer is to commit faster rather than to re-stack after his dash.
audit.corrected: An Acquired Taste stacks last 5 seconds from the last hit and decay one at a time; Spinning Slash buys him the time to let them run out.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: An Acquired Taste

audit.whatIsWrong: late and spikes[3] call Tahm Kench's W "Abyssal Voyage" and describe "global repositioning" that "lets you arrive at drakes and Baron".
audit.why: There is no such ability. Abyssal Dive is a 1.35s channel into a 1000-1200 range blink. A split-pushing Tryndamere is answered by rotating early on foot, not by a global that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Rotate early to objectives; Devour is what peels for your carries. Abyssal Dive is a telegraphed short-range engage.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive

audit.why: Anti-heal as a core item is right — Bloodlust heals up to 300 off consumed Fury on a 12s cooldown, and Battle Fury's passive gives him bonus attack damage scaling with missing health, so a chunked Tryndamere both hits harder and heals more.
sources: League Wiki — Tryndamere: Bloodlust, Battle Fury

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — Tongue Lash stuns Tryndamere mid-trade and Devour removes him from the fight before he can sustain back with Bloodlust.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — Tongue Lash stuns Tryndamere 1.5s mid-trade and he has no Spinning Slash yet to leave with, so the auto chain is free.

edits.before: Tryndamere's Undying Rage fully invalidates your Devour kill window — never swallow him after he pops R or you waste the combo and he walks out healthy.
edits.after: Undying Rage runs 5 seconds and Devour holds only 3 — and he can press R after you have already eaten him, so swallowing into an active Rage just spends your ult.

edits.before: Full-build Tryndamere with Undying Rage up is effectively unkillable in a duel — your job shifts entirely to Tongue Lash zoning and Abyssal Voyage team repositioning.
edits.after: Full-build Tryndamere with Undying Rage up is effectively unkillable in a duel — your job shifts to Tongue Lash zoning and eating him the moment Rage is on cooldown.

edits.before: Force all-ins only when Undying Rage is on cooldown — track the 100-second window so Devour produces a real kill
edits.after: Force all-ins only when Undying Rage is down — it is 120/100/80s, so at rank 1 one whiff buys you two whole minutes

edits.before: Use Spinning Slash through minions to dodge incoming Tongue Lash and reset the An Acquired Taste stack count
edits.after: Spinning Slash through minions to dodge Tongue Lash and stall until your An Acquired Taste stacks time out

edits.before: Pop Undying Rage the instant Devour animation begins so he survives the swallow and walks out at full Bloodlust stacks
edits.after: Pop Undying Rage even after Devour has him — it casts through the suppression and outlasts the 3s hold by two

edits.before: Use Mocking Shout to slow Tahm Kench and create the spacing needed to kite and crit without eating a stun
edits.after: Mocking Shout you as you walk away — the slow half lands only while your back is turned, so it punishes retreats

edits.before: At level 1 your Tongue Lash range lets you contest the wave and apply the first An Acquired Taste stack without ever walking into Tryndamere's auto range — poke the stack, back off, repeat. The moment you hit level 2 the stun threat is live: fish for the third stack with a slow into auto or second Tongue Lash and the stun locks him before Bloodlust Q can heal the trade back. He has no escape tool yet, so a stun into Devour at levels 2-3 is a clean chunk that costs him CS and health without any real answer on his side.
edits.after: At level 1 your Tongue Lash range lets you contest the wave and apply the first An Acquired Taste stack without ever walking into Tryndamere's auto range — poke the stack, back off, repeat. The moment you hit level 2 the stun threat is live: fish for the third stack with a slow into auto or second Tongue Lash and the 1.5-second stun locks him before Bloodlust Q can heal the trade back. He has no escape tool yet, so a stun into a full auto chain at levels 2-3 is a clean chunk that costs him CS and health without any real answer on his side.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where you must respect Spinning Slash — he can now dodge your Tongue Lash skillshot by dashing through a minion, and Mocking Shout slow makes it harder for you to close the gap to apply stacks in return. Play for the CS lead you built early and bait him into over-committing by looking vulnerable near minions. At level 6 the entire dynamic shifts around Undying Rage: treat the R cooldown as your kill timer, farm aggressively when it is down, and refuse to Devour him when it is active — swallowing a Tryndamere in R means five seconds of him regenerating Bloodlust stacks inside your belly while you do nothing.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where you must respect Spinning Slash — he dodges your Tongue Lash by dashing through a minion, and every crit shaves 1.5s off its 12/11/10/9/8s cooldown, so a long fight hands it back to him fast. Mocking Shout only slows you while your back is turned, so walking at him costs nothing; it is the retreat it punishes. At level 6 the entire dynamic shifts around Undying Rage: treat its 120/100/80s as your kill timer, farm aggressively when it is down, and refuse to Devour into an active Rage — your hold lasts 3 seconds and his Rage lasts 5, so the swallow has to land before the button.

edits.before: Late game Tryndamere with full crit is legitimately hard to kill, but that is fine — your job was never to assassinate him. Your Thick Skin grey health and stacked Heartsteel or Sunfire mean he cannot kill you either in a fair duel, and any moment he overextends without R up is still a death if you land the three-stack stun into Devour. Shift your energy to Abyssal Voyage: your global repositioning lets you arrive at drakes and Baron to peel your carries, and a Tryndamere who is stuck splitpushing against a tank he cannot kill is already losing the game on tempo.
edits.after: Late game Tryndamere with full crit is legitimately hard to kill, but that is fine — your job was never to assassinate him. Your Thick Skin grey health and stacked Heartsteel or Sunfire mean he cannot kill you either in a fair duel, and any moment he overextends without R up is still a death if you land the three-stack stun into Devour. Shift your energy to the map instead: rotate early to drakes and Baron so Devour is there to peel your carries, and a Tryndamere who is stuck splitpushing against a tank he cannot kill is already losing the game on tempo.

edits.before: Two stacks plus Tongue Lash slow sets up the level-2 stun: he has no Spinning Slash yet, so the combo lands cleanly and Devour costs him a full minion wave.
edits.after: Two stacks plus the Tongue Lash slow sets up the level-2 stun: he has no Spinning Slash yet, so the combo lands cleanly and costs him a full minion wave.

edits.before: Three stacks means a guaranteed stun into Devour — Tryndamere's Bloodlust Q cannot heal back a burst this large and he has no escape to break the lock.
edits.after: Three stacks means a guaranteed 1.5s stun and a free auto chain — he has no Spinning Slash yet, so nothing breaks the lock and Bloodlust arrives too late.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage is online but Undying Rage changes every kill condition: track the 100-second R cooldown and only commit the Devour combo in the window when it is down.
edits.after: Devour is online but Undying Rage changes every kill condition: it runs 120/100/80s, and your hold lasts 3 seconds against his 5 — commit only when Rage is down.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Out-last it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage (120/100/80s, 5 seconds of death immunity): Devour only holds for 3 seconds, so it can never out-last a Rage. - Spinning Slash (12/11/10/9/8s) drops 1.5s per crit on you.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Undying Rage: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If behind, farm safe and let your spikes re-open the lane.
edits.after: Trade around Undying Rage: with it down, run the full pattern. Mocking Shout only slows a turned back, so walking at him is free — it is retreating that costs you.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tryndamere's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour holds for 3 seconds; Undying Rage runs 5 and casts straight through it. Eat him before he presses R, never after.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Out-last it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 5s immune, and Devour holds only 3. Engage once Rage is spent.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Out-last it. When it is down — Q-AA + R him.
edits.after: Undying Rage runs 5s and casts through your suppression; Devour holds 3s. Eat him before he pops it.

notes: SYSTEMIC AUTHORING ERROR ACROSS THE CHAMPION, not just this matchup: the content layer repeatedly promises "stun into Devour" at levels 2-3, in this entry and in sion, sylas, teemo and trundle as well. Devour is Tahm Kench's ultimate and arrives at 6. Worth a champion-wide grep of champ-data/content/tahmkench.js for Devour mentioned in any Lvl 1-5 spike or in whys[0..3]. Same for the 182 "Abyssal Voyage" occurrences (pre-rework ultimate; current W is Abyssal Dive, no global). The packet's five suspectNames hits here are all false positives — "Three An Acquired Taste", "Use Spinning Slash", "Pop Undying Rage", "Use Mocking Shout" and "Stack An Acquired Taste" are all correct names with an ordinary verb in front of them. No WKM_LINES issues seen.
